full_judgment:
2. The plaint case, in brief, is that Din Mondal alias Dinu Mondal was the owner of the schedule suit land. Dinu Mondal died leaving behind his wife Dukhi Bewa and 2(two) daughters Sahachari and Gayahwari. According to Dayabhaga System of Hindu Law Dinu's wife Dukhi Bewa got life estate in the suit land left by him. Dukhi Bewa had no son and as such her elder daughter Sahachari was given in marriage with one Shreecharan Mondal and he was kept in her house as domesticated son-in-law. The suit land was recorded in CS khatian 177 in the name of Dukhi Bewa and Shreecharan Mondal to the extent of 8 annas share each but Shreecharan Mondal had no title over the suit land. During her possession and enjoyment Dukhi Bewa sold 0.37 acres from plot 70 to Surendar Chandra Sarker and others for the legal necessity and handed over possession thereof. Accordingly, the said 0.37 acres of land was recorded in SA khatian 346 and RS khatian 49 in the name of Surendra Chandra and others. Subsequently, Dukhi Bewa died leaving behind her 2(two) daughters Sahachari and Gayahwari Mondal. As per Dayabhaga system they got life interest in the land left by Dukhi Bewa except the land measuring 0.37 acres texhibitransferred by Dukhi. Gayashwari subsequently died leaving behind his only son Ashwani Kumar Mondal the father of defendants 1-3 and grandfather of defendants 4 and 5 and her sister Sahachari Mondal. In this way Sahachari Mondal acquired life interest over the property left by Dukhi Bewa measuring an area of 5.25 acres. Sahachari died leaving behind his 3(three) sons Kiron Mondal, Dinesh Mondal and Haripada Mondal and thus Ashwani, Kiron, Dinesh and Haripada Mondal acquired the suit land as grandson of Dinu Mondal in equal shares i.e., each of them got ¼ th of property measuring an area of 1.3125 acres. In SA operation SA khatian 345 in respect of 5.25 acres was recorded in the name of Gayasshari's husband Ananda Mondal and Sahachari's husband Shreecharan Mondal along with titleless Madhab Mondal and Profulla Kumar Mondal. In RS operation, RS khatian 15 measuring an area of 5.31 acres (0.06 acres land) was recorded 8 annas in the name of Gayasshari's son Ashwani Kumar and remaining 8 annas in the name of Kiron, Dinesh and Haripada, the sons of Sahachari. During their possession and enjoyment Ashwani Mondal transferred 0.65 acres to Kiron, Dinesh and Haripada by a registered kabala dated 1-11-1969 from RS Khatian 15 corresponding to SA khatian 345 and handed over possession thereof. Kiron, Dinesh and Horipada got 3.9375 acres by inheritance and also 0.6150 acres by purchase measuring total 4.5525 acres from SA khatian 345 corresponding to RS khatian 15. They sold 0.04 acres to defendants 20 and 21 and remained in possession in 4.5525 acres. During their possession and enjoyment Kiron Chandra died leaving behind his 2(two) sons Parimal and Nirmal plaintiffs 5 and 6; Dinesh, Haripada, Parimal and Nirmol during their possession and enjoyment over 4.5125 acres sold 0.63 acres to defendant 24 and remained in possession over 3.8825 acres. Haripada died leaving behind his 4(four) sons Maran Chandra Sarker, Bimal Chandra Sarker, Kamal Chandra Sarker and Sujan Chandra Sarker. In this way the plaintiffs have been owning and possessing 3.8825 acres by erecting houses thereon and planting trees. In 2004, the son of Gayahwari mutated his name in respect of the suit land showing his share to the extent 8 annas then it came to the knowledge of the plaintiffs and they filed an objection against the said mutation and it was cancelled in 2013. The defendants refused to partition the land showing the shares of the plaintiffs to the extent ¾ share of the total land then they instituted the suit praying for shaham over the land as detailed to the schedule of the plaint. 

 3. The defendants 1-5 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the statement made in the plaint. They contended that the suit is not maintainable in the present form and manner and it is barred by limitation. They further contended that Dukhi. Bewa was the owner of land measuring 5.62 acres. Dukhi Bewa had 2(two) daughters Sahachari and Gayashwari. The husband of Shahachari namely Shreecharan Mondal was kept in her house as domesticated son-in-law. CS khatian 177 was prepared wrongly showing 8 annas share to Dukhi and Sreecharan each but actually Dukhi Bewa was the owner of the total land. The defendant after examination of witnesses on 1-8-2018 amended the written statement and incorporated the fact that the suit property was owned by Dukhi Bewa as Yatuka at the time of her marriage and consequently it will be treated as her Stridhana. They admitted that Dukhi Bewa sold 0.37 acres of plot 70 to Surendra Chandra Sarker and others and during her possession and enjoyment on remaining land measuring 5.25 acres she gave her daughter Gayahwari to marriage with Ananda Mondal and kept him in her house as domesticated son-in-law. In 1940 she partitioned the land between his 2(two) daughters and each of the daughters got 2.625 acres. During possession and enjoyment through the husbands of 2(two) daughters SA record in respect of 5.25 acres was recorded in the name of Shreecharan and Ananda and erroneously the names of Madab Mondal and Profullo Mondal were included in the khatian but they have no title and possession over the suit land. Sahachari Mondal died leaving behind his 3(three) sons Kiron Chandra, Dinesh Chandra and Haripada and they inherited the property left by Sahachari in equal shares. Gayahwari died leaving behind her only son Ashwani Kumar Mandal and he inherited 8 annas share enjoyed by her mother. Ashwani during his possession and enjoyment transferred 0.28 acres to Minor Hossain, 0.15 acres to Montu Shah, 0.13 acres to Chondi Dash, Nipendranath and Raton Mondal and .24 acres to Md Rohman and others. Apart from the above transfer, he transferred 0.615 acres to the 3(three) sons of Sahachari Mondal i.e., the predecessors of the plaintiffs. Aashwani Kumar Mondal further sold 0.04 acres to defendant 3 and 0.285 acres to defendant 24. Thus he totally transferred 1.74 acres from the suit property and had been enjoying and possession of the remaining part. He mutated his name in the year 2004 to the extent of 8 annas share of the suit jote and died leaving behind the defendants 1-5 as heirs. The father of the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.132 of 2003 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Court No.4, Gazipur which was dismissed on 27-10-2005. The plaintiffs have no title and possession over the land measuring an area of 0.885 acres having been enjoyed by the defendants. The suit has been filed on false averments and as such it would be dismissed. 

 5. Mr Uzzal Bhowmick, learned Advocate for the appellants takes us through the materials on record and submits that the plaintiff although claimed that Dinu Mondal was the original owner of the suit land but they failed to lead any positive evidence supporting the contention. Admittedly CS record was prepared in the name of Dukhi Bewa showing his share to the extent of 8 annas. The presumption of preparation of CS record is to be rebuted by the plaintiff through evidence. Subsequently, 2(two) records were prepared in conformity of the CS record. In SA record the names of the husbands of 2(two) daughters of Dukhi Bewa were recorded with the name of some other title less persons and RS record was prepared in the name of Ashwini Kumar Mondal to the extent of 8 annas share which supports that Dukhi Bewa obtained the suit land as Yatuka and it was her stridhana. Although, the said claim of the defendants about Stridhana was incorporated by amended of the written statement at a belated stage but it was nothing but a better statement. The defendants proved their case by Exhibiting CS, SA and RS khatian Exhibits-Ka-Gha. He refers to the deed of purchase of the plaintiffs predecessor Exhibit-5 and submits that through the said documents the plaintiff processor purchased land from 3 plots to the extent of 8 arenas share of each plot. The plaintiffs thus admitted the title of 8 annas share of the defendant Ashwani over the suit land. While the sons of Sahachari admitted the title of the defendant to the extent of 8 annas share, their sons cannot undo those after expiry of long years. He refers to the statement of paragraph-Cha of the written statement and submits that Dukhi Bewa in the year 1940 partitioned of the suit land between his 2(two) daughters which has been admitted by PW2 and supported by the evidence of DW 4. The plaintiff did not deny it by cross-examining DW 4. The title and possession over the suit land has been admitted by the first generation, second generation and third generation, now the plaintiffs being fourth generation cannot disown it. The subsequent 2 records, i.e., SA and RS support the aforesaid partition by Dukhi Bewa. It is admitted position of fact that Ashwani Kumar being the son of Gayashwari transferred more than 4 annas share of the suit land. The plaintiffs' present suit without challenging those documents and claiming title over the suit land and without making any prayer for correction of the record of rights is not maintainable. The facts and circumstances and the transfer by Ashwani Kumar proves that he got the suit land per stripes. The trial Court without entering into the facts and evidence on record erred in law and thereby decreed the suit which is to be interfered with by this Court in this appeal. 

 6. Mr Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the respondents submits that the defendants totally failed to prove that the property in question was Stridhana of Dukhi Bewa. Their claim to get 8 annas of Dukhi Bewa's property by Ashwani son Gayashwari fails paving the way to success of the partition suit as claimed by the plaintiffs. He submits that in the original written statement the story of Stridhana was not stated but it was incorporated on 1-8-2018 after 7 years of the institution of the suit, i.e. after conclusion of the examination of the plaintiffs' witnesses. It clearly shows that this sort of amendment was afterthought and concocted. He refers to the provision of section 105 of the Code of Civil Procedure and submits that the plaintiff although did not challenge it to the higher Court at that time that and it was merged with the judgment but at this stage they can raise the port of allowing such sort of amendment. The trial Court also found that although the defendants predecessor Ashwani transferred his major share from the suit jote but suppressing those facts he mutated his name in the concerned office showing his share to the extent of 8 annas. He then submits that although in the written statement, the defendants contended that Dukhi Bewa gave the property to her two daughters in equal share whereby the property was partitioned by Dukhi Bewa herself during her lifetime but it has been consistently held by our Apex Court that mutual family arrangement for convenience of enjoyment of the property does not amount to partition. Moreover, since both Sahachari and Gayashwari owned and possessed the property as life estate but after death of both of them the property went to the legal heirs of original owner Dinu Mondal and they are Dinu Mondal's daughters' sons. The property admittedly stands recorded in RS khatian No.15 in the name of both parties. Although showing the shares wrongly in the name of Ashwani to the extent of 8 annas. This contention of the defendants is legally infirm and rightly rejected by the trial Court. He refers to the case of Probir Kumar Rakshit vs Abdus Sabur, 14 BLC (AD) 28; Rajendranath Saha @ Rajendra Pradan Saha and another vs Md Sonaullah Pramanik and others, 42 DLR 393 and Abdul Noor Q Cunnu Miah and another vs Makhan Miah Q Md Laisuzzaman and others, 12 MLR (AD) 347 and relied on the ratio laid therein. Mr Neogi then submits that earlier the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.132 of 2003 which was dismissed for default on 27-1-2005 and the cause of action for a partition suit being recurrent which exists till the property is partitioned by metes and bounds, the present partition suit is therefore squarely competent and maintainable. In the aforesaid premises the trial Court correctly decreed the suit which may not be interfered with by this Court.
